args.summary: checkout-api began failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) after the latest deploy. Current version v2.3.1 was unhealthy with an error rate of 18%. I rolled back all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release with a healthy production history. Post-rollback verification shows v2.3.0 active in all three regions, healthy, with error rate down to 0.2%. Root cause of the v2.3.1 failure is not yet known and needs investigation; the v2.3.1 release should be blocked from redeployment until it is fixed and validated. Note: v2.3.1-rc is unhealthy in staging, which is consistent with the production failure.

trace.final:
## Summary

**Rollback completed — checkout-api is healthy again.**

**State found:**
- All three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) were on **v2.3.1**, healthy: `false`, error rate **18%**.
- Release history showed v2.3.1 as `unhealthy` in production, and v2.3.1-rc also `unhealthy` in staging.

**Action taken:**
- Rolled back all production regions to **v2.3.0** — the most recent release with a healthy *production* record (v2.2.9 was also healthy but older).
- Verified after rollback: all three regions report v2.3.0, `healthy: true`, error rate down to **0.2%**.

**Incident:** Opened **INC-0001**, SEV2, on-call paged, describing the v2.3.1 health-check failure and the rollback to v2.3.0.

Two notes worth flagging:
- My first `create_incident` call timed out. Before retrying I checked `list_incidents`, which returned empty — so nothing was created and there was no risk of a duplicate page. I reused the same idempotency key for the retry as a further guard.
- I did **not** deploy anything new; this was a rollback to a version with a known-healthy production history, so no change-manager approval was required. **v2.3.1 should be treated as unsafe** — it failed identically to its staging RC, so the release candidate validation apparently didn't catch this. Root cause is still unknown and needs follow-up, and v2.3.1 should be blocked from redeployment until fixed and verified.
